headline: High: Perplexity can ingest uploaded content and browse externally, creating default-path leakage and cascading-error risk when paired with Authelia’s OAuth/ForwardAuth outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Perplexity can browse the web and analyze uploaded PDFs/images, so attacker-controlled content can enter its context. Authelia exposes OAuth 2.0/OpenID Connect and ForwardAuth outputs that could be forwarded into Perplexity by an operator. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than directly observed.
conditions: IF Authelia outputs are copied into Perplexity prompts or uploads
IF Perplexity is used to summarize untrusted web or document content
mitigations: Keep Authelia outputs out of Perplexity prompts
Use a fixed prompt template that strips instructions from pasted text
Review any uploaded document before analysis
Separate trusted admin workflows from research workflows
requires-engineering: add provenance labeling between tools

B_data_leakage.rationale: Perplexity touches search queries, uploaded documents, and browsing context, and its vendor-hosted backend can transmit that content externally. Authelia handles authentication flows via OAuth/OIDC and ForwardAuth, so if those outputs include identifiers or tokens, they can be exposed through Perplexity. The pairwise leak path is plausible but not directly documented.
conditions: IF Authelia-derived auth artifacts or user identifiers are pasted into Perplexity
IF uploaded documents contain secrets or regulated data
mitigations: Do not send tokens or session artifacts to Perplexity
Redact identifiers before upload
Use a separate tenant/account for sensitive research
Disable sharing of generated answers containing auth details
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on copied text

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress but no filesystem write, subprocess, or git mutation; Perplexity is vendor-hosted with no host execution, no filesystem write, and no git state changes. Their mutable-resource overlap is therefore limited, and the main conflict surface is only network/API usage, which is not enough for a higher severity.
conditions: IF both are wired to the same upstream API quota or rate-limited endpoint
IF an operator manually shares mutable credentials between them
mitigations: Use separate API credentials
Set per-tool rate limits
Avoid shared writable workspaces
Monitor for quota contention
requires-engineering: add orchestration locks for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity is explicitly an answer engine with live search and citations, so it may render or act on Authelia-derived outputs if an operator feeds them forward. Authelia can emit authentication-related results, and Perplexity’s browsing context can amplify any mistaken assumptions into polished but unverified answers. The pairwise handoff is plausible, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Authelia outputs are treated as authoritative input to Perplexity
IF Perplexity answers are used to configure authentication or access policy
mitigations: Require human verification of Authelia-derived facts
Ask Perplexity to cite primary sources only
Compare outputs against Authelia docs before action
Do not automate policy changes from generated text
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: Perplexity touches uploaded documents and browsing context under a vendor-hosted service, while Authelia is an open-source authentication component with no stated data classes touched. If regulated identity or document data flows from Authelia into Perplexity, residency and retention obligations can diverge. The other agent is cited because the compliance risk arises from the pairwise data path.
conditions: IF regulated identity data from Authelia is entered into Perplexity
IF the deployment requires a residency or retention policy that Perplexity does not match
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Perplexity
Use a local-only review path for sensitive auth data
Document retention expectations for copied content
Confirm vendor terms before use
requires-engineering: route regulated workflows to a compliant system
